notes.front: What is the segregation table in § 177.848?
notes.back: A table of hazard classes and divisions showing which may not be loaded, transported or stored together in the same vehicle or storage facility.
notes.explanation: Each cell is blank, an X or an O; the rule sets out what each one means for loading.
notes.example: Like a chart of foods that must not share a shelf, but for classes of hazardous material in a truck.
notes.evidence: Except as otherwise provided in this subchapter, hazardous materials must be stored, loaded or transported in accordance with the following table and other provisions of this section:
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.848(d), PDF p. 20

notes.front: May a highway carrier accept or transport a hazardous material without a shipping paper?
notes.back: No, unless the material is excepted from shipping paper requirements.
notes.explanation: The only way round it is for the material to be excepted from shipping paper requirements.
notes.evidence: A person may not accept a hazardous material for transportation or transport a hazardous material by highway unless that person has received a shipping paper prepared in accordance with part 172 of this subchapter or the material is excepted from shipping paper requirements under this subchapter.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.817(a), PDF p. 3

notes.front: A driver arrives to collect six drums of a Class 3 liquid (not a limited quantity). The shipper has no shipping paper ready and says it will email one later. What should the driver do?
notes.back: A: not accept the drums until a shipping paper prepared under part 172 has been received.
notes.choices:
A) Not accept them until a shipping paper has been received
B) Accept them if the drums are labelled
C) Accept them if the trip is under 150 miles
D) Accept them and wait for the email
notes.choicesExplained: B: labels do not replace the shipping paper. C: § 177.817 sets no distance allowance. D: § 177.817(a) requires the paper before acceptance.
notes.explanation: The carrier may not accept or transport the material without the shipping paper, unless the material is excepted, which it is not here.
notes.evidence: unless that person has received a shipping paper prepared in accordance with part 172 of this subchapter
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.817(a), PDF p. 3

notes.front: Which shipments may no one accept for transport by motor vehicle, under § 177.801?
notes.back: A forbidden material, or a hazardous material not prepared in accordance with the regulations.
notes.explanation: The duty falls on whoever accepts or transports, not only on the shipper who prepared it.
notes.evidence: No person may accept for transportation or transport by motor vehicle a forbidden material or hazardous material that is not prepared in accordance with the requirements of this subchapter.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.801, PDF p. 2

notes.front: Over what period must hazardous materials be transported without unnecessary delay?
notes.back: From the start of loading until final unloading at destination.
notes.explanation: Movement, and the loading and unloading around it, are all covered by the duty.
notes.evidence: All shipments of hazardous materials must be transported without unnecessary delay, from and including the time of commencement of the loading of the hazardous material until its final unloading at destination.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.800(d), PDF p. 2

notes.front: How must hazmat packages not permanently attached to a motor vehicle be loaded?
notes.back: Secured against shifting, including movement between packages, under conditions normally incident to transportation.
notes.explanation: Packages with valves or other fittings must also be loaded to minimise the chance of damage.
notes.evidence: must be secured against shifting, including relative motion between packages, within the vehicle on which it is being transported, under conditions normally incident to transportation. Packages having valves or other fittings must be loaded in a manner to minimize the likelihood of damage during transportation.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.834(a), PDF p. 5

notes.front: How must a package bearing package orientation markings be loaded?
notes.back: In accordance with the markings, and it must stay in the position they show throughout transportation.
notes.explanation: The package must keep that position for the whole journey, not only at loading.
notes.evidence: must be loaded on a transport vehicle or within a freight container in accordance with such markings and must remain in the correct position indicated by the markings during transportation.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.834(b), PDF p. 5

notes.front: A loader lays boxes marked with orientation arrows on their sides so more fit, and leaves a gap so they can slide. Which requirement is broken?
notes.back: A: both: the boxes must follow their orientation markings and be secured against shifting.
notes.choices:
A) Both the orientation rule and the rule against shifting
B) Only the orientation rule
C) Only the rule against shifting
D) Neither, if the trip is short
notes.choicesExplained: B: leaving the boxes free to slide breaks § 177.834(a) too. C: laying marked boxes on their sides breaks § 177.834(b) too. D: neither rule depends on distance.
notes.explanation: § 177.834(a) and (b) each apply: secure against shifting, and keep marked packages in the position the markings show.
notes.evidence: Each package containing a hazardous material bearing package orientation markings prescribed in § 172.312 of this subchapter must be loaded on a transport vehicle or within a freight container in accordance with such markings
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.834(a)–(b), PDF p. 5

notes.front: While loading or unloading which materials is smoking on or about a motor vehicle forbidden?
notes.back: Class 1 (explosive), Class 3 (flammable liquid), Class 4 (flammable solid), Class 5 (oxidizing) and Division 2.1 (flammable gas).
notes.explanation: The rule covers the area on or about the vehicle, during both loading and unloading.
notes.evidence: Smoking on or about any motor vehicle while loading or unloading any Class 1 (explosive), Class 3 (flammable liquid), Class 4 (flammable solid), Class 5 (oxidizing), or Division 2.1 (flammable gas) materials is forbidden.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.834(c), PDF p. 5

notes.front: A forklift driver lights a cigarette beside the trailer while unloading Division 5.1 bags. Is that allowed?
notes.back: D: no; smoking on or about the vehicle is forbidden while loading or unloading Class 5 materials.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, because oxidizers do not burn
B) Yes, if the driver stands more than a metre away
C) Yes, because the rule covers loading only
D) No, smoking is forbidden while loading or unloading Class 5
notes.choicesExplained: A: Class 5 is named in § 177.834(c). B: the rule says “on or about” the vehicle, with no distance allowance. C: the rule covers loading and unloading.
notes.explanation: Class 5 (oxidizing) is on the § 177.834(c) list, and the rule covers unloading as well as loading.
notes.evidence: Extreme care shall be taken in the loading or unloading of any Class 1 (explosive), Class 3 (flammable liquid), Class 4 (flammable solid), Class 5 (oxidizing), or Division 2.1 (flammable gas) materials
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.834(c)–(d), PDF p. 5

notes.front: To which packaged materials does the segregation rule in § 177.848 apply?
notes.back: Materials in packages that must be labelled or placarded under part 172.
notes.explanation: The test is whether the package must be labelled or placarded, not whether the vehicle is placarded.
notes.evidence: This section applies to materials which meet one or more of the hazard classes defined in this subchapter and are: (1) In packages that must be labeled or placarded in accordance with part 172 of this subchapter;
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.848(a), PDF p. 19

notes.front: A van carries 200 kg of labelled Class 3 cans and 100 kg of labelled Division 5.1 bags, too little to need placards. Does § 177.848 segregation apply?
notes.back: B: yes; the packages must be labelled, so segregation applies even though placards are not required.
notes.choices:
A) No, because the van needs no placards
B) Yes, because the packages must be labelled
C) No, because segregation is only for bulk
D) Only if the trip crosses a state line
notes.choicesExplained: A: § 177.848(a)(1) says labelled or placarded, so labelled packages are enough. C: the rule applies to packages, not only bulk. D: the section has no such limit.
notes.explanation: Segregation turns on the packages needing labels or placards, not on the vehicle needing placards.
notes.evidence: In packages that must be labeled or placarded in accordance with part 172 of this subchapter;
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.848(a)(1), PDF p. 19

notes.front: What does a blank space, or the absence of a class, mean in the segregation table?
notes.back: No restrictions apply.
notes.explanation: Only an X or an O imposes a restriction on loading two classes together.
notes.evidence: The absence of any hazard class or division or a blank space in the table indicates that no restrictions apply.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.848(e)(1), PDF p. 22

notes.front: What does an X mean in the segregation table?
notes.back: The materials may not be loaded, transported or stored together in the same transport vehicle or storage facility during transportation.
notes.explanation: Unlike an O, no method of separation makes an X combination acceptable.
notes.evidence: The letter ‘‘X’’ in the table indicates that these materials may not be loaded, transported, or stored together in the same transport vehicle or storage facility during the course of transportation.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.848(e)(2), PDF p. 22

notes.front: What does an O mean in the segregation table?
notes.back: The materials may not travel together unless separated so that, if packages leak in normal transport, they could not mix.
notes.explanation: An O allows loading together only with that separation in place.
notes.evidence: unless separated in a manner that, in the event of leakage from packages under conditions normally incident to transportation, commingling of hazardous materials would not occur.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.848(e)(3), PDF p. 22

notes.front: The segregation table shows an X where Division 2.1 meets Division 2.3 Zone A. A shipper wants to load both on one truck, with pallets between them. Allowed?
notes.back: A: no; X means they may not be loaded, transported or stored together in the same vehicle.
notes.choices:
A) No, an X forbids them in the same vehicle
B) Yes, pallets are enough separation
C) Yes, if both are under 454 kg
D) Yes, if they are loaded at different facilities
notes.choicesExplained: B: separation is the remedy for an O, not an X. C: the table has no weight allowance. D: the X applies to the vehicle, wherever each item was loaded.
notes.explanation: Separation helps only with an O; an X forbids the combination in one vehicle.
notes.evidence: The letter ‘‘X’’ in the table indicates that these materials may not be loaded, transported, or stored together in the same transport vehicle
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.848(d)–(e), PDF p. 22

notes.front: In the segregation table, Class 3 and Division 5.1 meet at an O. How may drums of each travel in one trailer?
notes.back: A: only if separated so that, should packages leak in normal transport, the materials could not mix.
notes.choices:
A) Only if separated so leaks could not mix
B) Freely, with no conditions
C) Only if each is under 454 kg
D) Never in the same trailer
notes.choicesExplained: B: an O is a restriction; a blank would mean no restriction. C: the table sets no weight allowance. D: that is the meaning of an X, not an O.
notes.explanation: An O is conditional: the combination is allowed with separation that prevents commingling.
notes.evidence: The letter ‘‘O’’ in the table indicates that these materials may not be loaded, transported, or stored together in the same transport vehicle or storage facility during the course of transportation unless separated
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.848(d)–(e), PDF p. 22

notes.front: The segregation table cell for Class 3 and Class 8 liquids is blank. What does that mean for loading them together?
notes.back: D: no restriction from the table applies.
notes.choices:
A) They may never share a vehicle
B) They must be separated so leaks could not mix
C) Only the Class 8 may be carried
D) No restriction from the table applies
notes.choicesExplained: A: that would be an X. B: that would be an O. C: a blank cell restricts neither material.
notes.explanation: A blank cell means the table puts no restriction on the pair.
notes.evidence: The absence of any hazard class or division or a blank space in the table indicates that no restrictions apply.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.848(e)(1), PDF p. 22

notes.front: What is the difference between an X and an O in the segregation table?
notes.back: X: never together in the same vehicle or storage facility. O: together only when separated so leaking packages could not mix.
notes.explanation: Both restrict loading; only the O can be satisfied by the way the load is separated.
notes.evidence: may not be loaded, transported, or stored together in the same transport vehicle or storage facility during the course of transportation unless separated in a manner that, in the event of leakage from packages under conditions normally incident to transportation, commingling of hazardous materials would not occur.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.848(e)(2)–(3), PDF p. 22

notes.front: Whatever separation is used, where may Class 8 (corrosive) liquids not be loaded?
notes.back: Above or adjacent to Class 4 (flammable) or Class 5 (oxidizing) materials.
notes.explanation: Shippers may load truckload shipments of these together when it is known the mixture would not cause fire or a dangerous evolution of heat or gas.
notes.evidence: Notwithstanding the methods of separation employed, Class 8 (corrosive) liquids may not be loaded above or adjacent to Class 4 (flammable) or Class 5 (oxidizing) materials; except that shippers may load truckload shipments of such materials together when it is known that the mixture of contents would not cause a fire or a dangerous evolution of heat or gas.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.848(e)(3), PDF p. 22

notes.front: Under § 177.848(c), which two pairings may not be stored, loaded and transported together?
notes.back: Cyanides with acids, if mixing would generate hydrogen cyanide; and Division 4.2 materials with Class 8 liquids.
notes.explanation: The acid pairing is barred only if the mixture would generate hydrogen cyanide.
notes.evidence: cyanides, cyanide mixtures or § 177.848 solutions may not be stored, loaded and transported with acids if a mixture of the materials would generate hydrogen cyanide; Division 4.2 materials may not be stored, loaded and transported with Class 8 liquids;
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.848(c), PDF p. 20

notes.front: A load plan puts drums of a Division 4.2 material next to drums of a Class 8 liquid, separated by an empty pallet. Is that acceptable?
notes.back: C: no; § 177.848(c) says Division 4.2 materials may not be stored, loaded and transported with Class 8 liquids.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, if the Class 8 is loaded on top
B) Yes, an empty pallet is enough separation
C) No, Division 4.2 may not travel with Class 8 liquids
D) Yes, if both are under 454 kg
notes.choicesExplained: A: placing Class 8 liquids above makes no difference to a prohibited pairing. B: § 177.848(c) forbids the pairing, not just mixing through leaks. D: no weight allowance applies.
notes.explanation: Paragraph (c) is a flat prohibition, so separation within the vehicle does not make it acceptable.
notes.evidence: Division 4.2 materials may not be stored, loaded and transported with Class 8 liquids;
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.848(c), PDF p. 20

notes.front: When must segregation for a subsidiary hazard be applied?
notes.back: When the package must bear a subsidiary hazard label and that segregation is more restrictive than the primary hazard’s.
notes.explanation: The more restrictive of the two segregations is the one applied.
notes.evidence: segregation appropriate to the subsidiary hazard must be applied when that segregation is more restrictive than that required by the primary hazard.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 177 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 177.848(e)(6), PDF p. 22
